Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:10:1.hebrew: האי תנה את אשתי את מיכל - דמשמע: זו אשתי, ולא מירב אשתי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:10:1.english: This [verse]: “Deliver me my wife Michal” - Which implies: This [one] is my wife, and Merab is not my wife.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:10:2.hebrew: מאי דריש ביה - רבי יוסי, דלא דריש "ולא מירב אשתי":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:10:2.english: What does he derive from it? - [Meaning,] Rabbi Yosei, who does not derive: “And Merab was not my wife.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:10:3.hebrew: לטעמיה - דדריש ממקרא מעורבב, כדלקמן: מה מיכל אשתי, אף מירב אשתי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:10:3.english: [Conforms] to his reasoning - For he expounds from a mixed verse, as [explained] below: Just as Michal [is] my wife, so too Merab [was] my wife.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:12:1.hebrew: קדושי מיכל לפלטי - פשיטא לן דבעבירה, דהא כתיב "אשתי מיכל", וקיימא לן (קידושין דף מז.) דעתיה אפרוטה, דבת קידושין היא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:12:1.english: Michal’s betrothal to Palti - It is obvious to us that [it was] in transgression, for behold, it is written: “[Deliver me] my wife Michal” (II Samuel 3:14), and we maintain (Kiddushin 47a) that his intention is on the peruta, so that she was [validly] betrothed [to David].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:15:1.hebrew: ואשתו היהודית - בכלב בן יפונה משתעי קרא. יהודית — על שם שכפרה בע"ז ונתגיירה, שכל הכופר בע"ז נקרא יהודי, דכתיב (דניאל ג׳:י״ב): איתי גוברין יהודאין וגו':
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:15:1.english: And his wife Hajehudijah - The verse is speaking of Caleb son of Jephunneh. [She is called] Yehudit [the Jewess] because she renounced idolatry and converted, for anyone who renounces idolatry is called a Jew, as it is written (Daniel 3:12): “There are certain Jewish men,” etc.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:15:2.english: Jered the father of Gedor - All of them are names of Moses.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:15:3.english: Mered - [This is] Caleb, who rebelled against the counsel of the spies.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:17:1.hebrew: תולדות אהרן ומשה - ומפרש בתריה בני אהרן, ולא הוזכרו בני משה שם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:17:1.english: The generations of Aaron and Moses - And [the verse] specifies after it the sons of Aaron, and the sons of Moses were not mentioned there.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:18:1.hebrew: שפדאו מצער גידול בנים - שהוטל עליו טורח השבטים, שעל אברהם היה מוטל אותו טורח, דכתיב (בראשית כ״ו:ד׳) והרביתי את זרעך — והוא פדאו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:18:1.english: That he redeemed him from the suffering of raising children - For the burden of [raising] the tribes was placed upon him, as that burden had been incumbent upon Abraham, as it is written: “And I will multiply your seed” (Genesis 26:4) — and he redeemed him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:1:1.hebrew: נפנה - שמעון לימינו, לידע אם יאמרו כמותו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:1:1.english: He turned - Shimon [turned] to his right, to know whether they would say as he [did].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:1:2.english: They cast down their faces - For they were afraid of him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:1:3.english: Master of thoughts - The Holy One, blessed be He.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:20:1.english: But isn’t it written: “Her husband”? - This implies that he had relations with her.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:20:2.english: That he became like a husband to her - For he cared for her and cherished her.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:20:3.english: Weeping as he went after her - [The Gemara] cites this as a challenge.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:20:4.english: To Bahurim - [The Gemara] continues expounding the verse.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:21:1.hebrew: תוקפו של יוסף ענוותנותו של בועז - דבר גדול של יוסף כדבר קל וקטן שבבועז. תוקף — דבר גדול וחמור, ויש לו שם; ענוה — דבר שאין לו שם, שאדם עושה לפי תומו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:21:1.english: Joseph’s power is the humility of Boaz - A great deed of Joseph is like an easy and minor matter for Boaz. "Power" [denotes] a great and formidable matter, which has renown; "humility" [denotes] a matter that has no renown, which a person does unassumingly.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:21:2.english: That his flesh became - [His sexual] organ.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:21:3.hebrew: כראשי לפתות - נתקשה, ואעפ"כ כבש יצרו, ואף על פי שפנויה היתה ועמו במיטה. אבל יוסף — אשת איש היתה, ואינה עמו במיטה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:21:3.english: Like the heads of turnips - [His organ] became erect, and nevertheless he subdued his inclination, even though she was an unmarried woman and with him in bed. But [in the case of] Joseph, she was a married woman, and she was not with him in bed.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:2:1.english: Nor do they perform ḥalitza with his wife - Because she is forbidden to marry [anyone else].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:2:2.hebrew: חליצה גנאי היא לו, לבא <abbr title="לבית דין">לב"ד</abbr> ותהא רוקקת לפניו; וייבום גנאי הוא לו, לקום על שם אחיו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:2:2.english: Ḥalitza is a disgrace for him, to come to court and have her spit before him; and levirate marriage [yibum] is a disgrace for him, to succeed to his brother’s name.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:2:3.hebrew: הא דרב אשי, בפ' קמא דקידושין (דף לב:):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:2:3.english: This [statement] of Rav Ashi is in the first chapter of Kiddushin (32b).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:3:1.hebrew: הראויות לו - המותרות לו, אבל נשיו של שאול לא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:3:1.english: Appropriate for him - [Those] permitted to him, but the wives of Saul [were] not.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:6:1.hebrew: מלוה אית לך גבאי - עושר גדול, וקידושין אחרים לא קיבלתי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:6:1.english: You have a loan in my possession - [Namely, the] great riches [that I owe you], and I received no other betrothal [payment from you].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:7:1.hebrew: בעת תת - כשהגיע עת לתתה לדוד, נתנה לעדריאל:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:7:1.english: At the time when [she] was to be given - When the time arrived to give her to David, he gave her to Adriel.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:7:2.hebrew: מלוה ופרוטה - מלוה — עושר גדול שנתחייבתי לך בשביל גלית, ופרוטה — שוה כסף שקבלתי ממך בהללו ערלות פלשתים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:7:2.english: A loan and a peruta - “A loan” — [the] great wealth that I became obligated [to give] you on account of Goliath; and “a peruta” — [the] monetary value that I received from you with these foreskins of the Philistines.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:8:1.hebrew: שאול סבר דעתיה - דמקדש, למקדש במלוה, דחשיבא. הלכך, לאו קידושי נינהו, ואזל ויהבה לפלטי בן ליש:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:8:1.english: Saul reasoned [that] his mind - [That the intention] of the one betrothing [is] to betroth with the loan, which is significant. Therefore, it is not a [valid] betrothal, and he went and gave her to Palti ben Laish.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:8:2.hebrew: ודוד סבר - דעתיה אפרוטה, משום הכי קרי לה אשתי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19b:8:2.english: And David reasoned - [The groom's] mind is on the peruta; that is why he called her "my wife."

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19b:18:1.hebrew: שפדאו מצער גידול בנים - פי' הקונטרס: גידול י"ב שבטים. ולא נהירא: חדא, דאינו צער אלא שמחה, כדאמרינן (ברכות דף סג.) גבי עובד אדום, שברכו ה' בבנים בשכר הארון שהיה בביתו; ועוד, דאברהם היו לו בנים מקטורה. וצריך לומר: צער של יוסף ואחיו, וגלגול ירידת מצרים:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19b:18:1.english: That he redeemed him from the suffering of raising children - The Kuntres Rashi explained: The raising of the twelve tribes. And this does not appear correct: First, for it is not suffering, but rather joy, as we say (Berakhot 63a) regarding Obed-Edom, that the Lord blessed him with children as a reward for the Ark that was in his house; and furthermore, Abraham also had children from Keturah. And one must say: It refers to the sorrow of Joseph and his brothers, and the chain of events leading to the descent into Egypt.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19b:2:1.hebrew: מצוה שאני - וכה"ג לא משני הש"ס גבי המלך שעבר לפני כלה בפרק האשה שנתארמלה (כתובות דף טז.), דמשני: פרשת דרכים הואי; ואמאי לא משני "מצוה שאני"? וי"ל, דהתם אין המצוה כי אם בשביל כבוד החתן והכלה, וכבוד מלך עדיף טפי מכבוד החתן, וא"כ ליכא מצוה; אבל הכא גבי יבום, מצוה איכא:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19b:2:1.english: A mitzva is different - And the Gemara does not answer in this manner regarding the king who passed before a bride in the chapter [entitled] HaIsha Shenit’armela (Ketubot 16b), where it answers [instead] that it was a crossroads; and why does it not answer [there], "A mitzva is different"? And it can be answered that there, the mitzva is only for the sake of the honor of the groom and the bride, and the honor of a king takes greater precedence than the honor of the groom, and if so, there is no mitzva; but here regarding levirate marriage [yibum], there is a mitzva.
